evidence.threat_model_doc: docs/INVARIANTS.md lines 69-87 explicitly scope guard as speed-bump against automation; defers (a) plugin-cache isolation and (b) code-review+CI for intentional rewrites

threat_model_rationale: INVARIANTS.md L69-87 honestly acknowledges the self-referential limit (guard source is itself editable in this repo) and delegates (1) intentional guard-source rewrites to plugin-cache isolation (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} read-only at deploy time) and (2) bypass detection to PR review + bats/shellcheck CI as a 2nd defense line. The guard's stated mission is 'block accidental/easy weakening by automation' — exactly what RESIDUAL-4/5/6 tests now cover semantically (jq-based command extraction, line-anchored exit2 count, deny() body integrity via awk). This is a principled scope statement, not an excuse: every threat *inside* the documented model (auto-loop lowering thresholds, removing patterns, deleting tests, disabling registration, neutralizing exit2 via comments or function-body rewrites) is now blocked deterministically.
